claims.text: A compositionally tuned high-entropy alloy containing Nb, Mo, and Ta will exhibit superconductivity at cryogenic temperatures.
Nb, Mo, and Ta are superconductivity-promoting alloying elements in the proposed HEA.
Optimizing electron count enhances electron-phonon coupling in the proposed HEA.
The proposed initial HEA is an as-synthesized homogeneous alloy with a balanced mixture of refractory and superconductivity-prone elements.
The proposed alloy is intended to operate as a superconductor under ambient pressure.
Systematic compositional tuning and high-throughput synthesis will be used to identify superconducting HEA compositions.
Transport, magnetic-susceptibility, and first-principles electron-phonon calculations will be combined to evaluate candidate compositions.
Measurements below 30 K can capture the proposed superconducting transitions.
The superconducting alloy will have a single-phase, homogeneous solid-solution microstructure.
A homogeneous single-phase microstructure minimizes scattering caused by inhomogeneities.
A homogeneous single-phase microstructure maximizes spatially uniform electron-phonon interactions.
Enhanced electron-phonon coupling facilitates Cooper-pair formation.
Cooper-pair formation produces a superconducting transition at low temperature.
The proposed alloy will show a sharp decrease in electrical resistance and a diamagnetic susceptibility signal below its critical temperature.
The superconducting transition may occur between 5 K and 20 K.
Similar HEAs lacking the specified compositional tuning do not exhibit superconductivity.
Superconductivity requires a narrow compositional window that optimizes electron count and lattice vibrational properties.
Compositions outside the optimal window may fail to produce a sharp superconducting transition.
